questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the right thoracic dermatome. He had chickenpox at age 8. The drug of choice for this condition in an immunocompetent patient is:
questions.exp: Valacyclovir 1g TDS for 7 days is preferred for herpes zoster in immunocompetent adults due to better bioavailability and dosing convenience compared to acyclovir.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man from a rural area presents with painless ulcer on glans penis for 3 weeks. Dark-field microscopy of the serous discharge shows motile spirochetes. The treatment of choice is:
opts: Benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis is best treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose, which achieves treponemicidal levels for over 4 weeks.

questions.q: A 40-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops acute tender erythematous nodules over the face and extensor surfaces of limbs, associated with fever and joint pain. Slit-skin smear shows BI of 4+. The most appropriate management is:
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 lepra reaction) in lepromatous leprosy is best managed with thalidomide 400mg/day (drug of choice), though prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated (women of childbearing age).

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense blisters over the lower abdomen and thighs, with sparing of mucous membranes. Nikolsky sign is negative. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense blisters, negative Nikolsky sign, mucosal sparing, and DIF showing linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. Target antigen is BPAG2 (BP180).

questions.q: A patient presents with well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk. Slit-skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows granuloma formation with Langhans giant cells and lymphocytes. The type of leprosy is:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy shows well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches with negative smear and granuloma with Langhans giant cells on biopsy, indicating high cell-mediated immunity.

questions.q: A 22-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with multiple painless, flesh-colored umbilicated papules on the face and genitals. CD4 count is 80 cells/μL. The causative agent belongs to:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a member of the Poxviridae family. It is common in immunosuppressed patients including HIV/AIDS.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias on the nose that has been growing slowly for 2 years. Biopsy shows palisading nuclei at the periphery of tumor islands. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Nodular basal cell carcinoma on the nose (high-risk area for recurrence) is best treated with Mohs micrographic surgery, which has the highest cure rate and maximizes tissue preservation.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with butterfly-shaped erythema on the face, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is strongly positive. The most specific antibody for this condition is:
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibody is the most specific antibody for SLE, though anti-dsDNA is both sensitive and specific and correlates with disease activity/nephritis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with tinea capitis with a boggy, fluctuant, painful mass on the scalp with broken-off hair stubs. Multiple openings exude pus on pressure. Regional lymphadenopathy is present. This condition is called:
questions.exp: Kerion celsi is an inflammatory form of tinea capitis caused most commonly by Trichophyton verrucosum or T. mentagrophytes, presenting as a boggy, painful mass with pustules and alopecia.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with a cauliflower-like warty plaque on the dorsum of the foot. Histopathology shows copper-penny bodies (sclerotic cells) with transverse septation. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is characterized by sclerotic (Medlar/copper-penny) bodies in tissue. It presents as warty plaques and is caused by dematiaceous fungi (Fonsecaea pedrosoi most commonly).

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman with generalized pruritus presents with excoriations and linear streaks in web spaces of fingers, wrists, and umbilical area. Family members are similarly affected. The drug of choice is:
questions.exp: Permethrin 5% cream is the drug of choice for scabies. It is applied to the entire body from neck down, left for 8-12 hours, and is safe in children above 2 months and in pregnancy.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male presents with foul-smelling, necrotic ulcers on the lower legs with undermined edges. Gram stain reveals Gram-negative rods. The wound exudes a sweet, fruity odor. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Pseudomonas aeruginosa produces a characteristic sweet, fruity (grape-like) odor due to 2-aminoacetophenone. It is commonly associated with wounds in diabetic patients and immunocompromised hosts.

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with intensely pruritic vesicular eruption symmetrically distributed over the elbows, knees, and sacrum. Biopsy shows neutrophil microabscesses at dermal papilla tips. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papillae. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is treated with dapsone for immediate relief and a strict gluten-free diet as long-term management, which may allow eventual tapering of dapsone.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasias, and calcinosis cutis. She has difficulty swallowing. Autoantibody most likely to be positive is:
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome: Calcinosis, Raynaud, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasias). Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc.

questions.q: A 32-year-old presents with well-demarcated, silvery-scaly plaques over the elbows and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. He also has nail pitting and onycholysis. Which cytokine is primarily responsible for the pathogenesis?
questions.exp: IL-17A, produced by Th17 cells, is the primary driver of psoriatic inflammation. IL-23 drives Th17 differentiation. Biologic agents targeting IL-17A (secukinumab, ixekizumab) and IL-23 are highly effective.

questions.q: A 28-year-old software engineer presents with chronic pruritic flexural eczema since childhood, allergic rhinitis, and asthma. Family history of atopy is positive. The serum IgE is elevated. The pathogenic mutation most commonly associated is:
questions.exp: Loss-of-function mutations in the filaggrin (FLG) gene impair the skin barrier, leading to increased transepidermal water loss and sensitization to allergens, predisposing to atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 19-year-old college student presents with painful ulcer with soft base, undermined edges, and highly contagious purulent discharge on the genitalia. Regional inguinal lymphadenopathy is present. Gram stain shows 'school of fish' pattern of Gram-negative rods. Diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, presents with painful soft ulcer with undermined edges, and Gram stain shows characteristic 'school of fish' or 'railroad tracks' pattern.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with progressive skin thickening, hyperpigmentation, and anhidrosis following multiple injections. She also has diffuse alopecia. The most likely diagnosis of the underlying cause is:
questions.exp: Morphea (localized scleroderma) can occur at injection sites. It presents with skin thickening, hyperpigmentation, and may cause alopecia when on the scalp. Unlike systemic sclerosis, it has no systemic involvement.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with flesh-colored, dome-shaped papule on the sole of the foot that disrupts dermatoglyphics. Black dots (thrombosed capillaries) are visible on paring. Causative HPV type is:
questions.exp: Plantar warts (verruca plantaris) are caused by HPV types 1 (deep, painful myrmecia type) and HPV 2 (mosaic type). HPV 6/11 cause anogenital warts; HPV 16/18 cause high-grade dysplasia.

questions.q: A dermatology resident is performing Wood's lamp examination. A patient with tinea versicolor shows which color under Wood's lamp?
questions.exp: Tinea versicolor (Malassezia furfur) shows yellow-green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Coral red is seen in erythrasma (Corynebacterium minutissimum). Golden yellow is in tinea capitis (Microsporum species).

questions.q: A 65-year-old fair-skinned man presents with a rapidly enlarging dome-shaped nodule with central keratinous crater over the nose. It developed over 6 weeks. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cells with keratin pearls but no significant atypia. Most likely diagnosis:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma is a rapidly growing lesion with a central keratin-filled crater that typically involutes spontaneously. Histologically it may be difficult to distinguish from SCC. Treatment is excision.

questions.q: Methotrexate is used in psoriasis. The most common serious long-term side effect requiring monitoring is:
questions.exp: Methotrexate causes dose-cumulative hepatotoxicity leading to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis. Liver biopsy is recommended after a cumulative dose of 3.5-4g in most protocols. Weekly folinic acid reduces hematologic side effects.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine for DLE is scheduled for ophthalmological review. The main ocular toxicity to screen for is:
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine can cause irreversible retinopathy with characteristic bull's eye maculopathy. Annual ophthalmological screening (OCT and visual field testing) is recommended after 5 years of use.

questions.q: A 12-year-old boy presents with a single painless patch of alopecia on the scalp. On dermoscopy, comma-shaped hairs, corkscrew hairs, and broken hairs are seen. KOH examination shows endothrix pattern. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Endothrix pattern (spores within hair shaft) is caused by Trichophyton tonsurans (most common in black dot tinea capitis) and T. violaceum. Ectothrix is caused by Microsporum species.

questions.q: A 55-year-old farmer presents with painless, progressive swelling of the foot with multiple sinuses discharging white granules. X-ray shows 'punched-out' bony lesions. The diagnosis is eumycetoma. The most appropriate treatment is:
questions.exp: Eumycetoma (caused by true fungi such as Madurella mycetomatis) is treated with long-term itraconazole. Surgery combined with antifungals may be needed in advanced cases. Actinomycetoma (bacterial) is treated with streptomycin + dapsone.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, and pathergy test positivity. The diagnosis is Behcet's disease. HLA association is:
questions.exp: Behcet's disease is strongly associated with HLA-B51 (particularly in populations along the Silk Road). Pathergy is a characteristic feature where skin prick causes papule/pustule formation after 24-48 hours.

questions.q: A 42-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with rapidly developing flesh-colored to violaceous plaques on the lower limbs. CD4 count is 50/μL. Biopsy shows proliferating spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces. The causative virus is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8/KSHV). It is most commonly AIDS-associated in advanced immunosuppression. Treatment includes ART optimization, intralesional vinblastine, or systemic chemotherapy.

questions.q: During a procedure, the dermatologist applies 88% trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to the skin. The depth of penetration achieved is:
questions.exp: 88% TCA penetrates to the reticular dermis (deep peel). 10-35% TCA reaches the superficial papillary dermis, 35-50% reaches mid-papillary to papillary-reticular junction, and 65-88% reaches the reticular dermis.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with brown macules on sun-exposed areas that worsen with pregnancy and OCP use. Dermoscopy shows both epidermal and dermal pigmentation. Wood's lamp shows enhancement in the epidermal component. Treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Melasma (mixed type) is best treated with triple combination cream (Kligman's formula) containing hydroquinone, tretinoin, and a mid-potency steroid along with strict photoprotection.

questions.q: A histopathology report describes 'saw-tooth' pattern of epidermal hyperplasia, hypergranulosis, and colloid (Civatte) bodies at the dermo-epidermal junction, along with a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate. This is characteristic of:
questions.exp: Lichen planus shows sawtooth acanthosis, hypergranulosis (responsible for Wickham's striae), colloid (Civatte) bodies from degenerating keratinocytes, and a band-like T-lymphocyte infiltrate at the DEJ.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman on long-term minocycline for acne presents with blue-gray discoloration of the skin, especially on sun-exposed areas and acne scars. The mechanism of this pigmentation is:
opts: Iron-melanin or iron-hemosiderin complexes deposited in dermis
questions.exp: Minocycline-induced pigmentation involves deposition of insoluble complexes of iron-melanin or iron-hemosiderin in the dermis. Three types are described based on distribution (Type I: previous inflammatory lesions; Type II: normal skin; Type III: diffuse muddy pigmentation).
